A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRAMER study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary materials are readable and can be matched despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original FRAMER benchmark results, component ablations, training analyses, computational measurements, and a 15-participant user study covering 30 scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds adaptive-weight analyses and evaluations with TSD-SR and SupResDiffGA.

M1.justification: Section 3.4, Equation 5 replaces softmax over LF/HF discrepancies with independent weights w_LF=1/(1+Delta_LF) and w_HF=1/(1+Delta_HF). This reverses the weighting preference toward smaller discrepancies and removes the sum-to-one coupling, substantially revising a core training component. The PDFs establish a changed reported rule, without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The training datasets and four Real-ISR evaluation datasets in Section 4.1 are unchanged. New Appendix D reuses RealSR and RealLQ250; its additional model configurations do not introduce different data or task requirements.

E2.justification: New Table 7 adds TSD-SR and SupResDiffGA as evaluated baselines, each compared with its FRAMER-equipped counterpart on two datasets. This substantially broadens the comparison to explicitly identified one-step and GAN-augmented diffusion systems. Existing benchmark and user-study comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces evaluations under two additional model/training configurations, stating that each baseline and FRAMER counterpart use matched training protocols. Appendix C additionally examines early and late training phases. Existing resolutions, scaling factor, metrics, degradation settings, and user-study design are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C extends the existing adaptive-module analyses with early/late layer-wise weight plots in Figure 9 and two image-level component comparisons with perceptual scores in Figure 10. Existing objective, teacher, negative-selection, frequency-assignment, and adaptive-module ablations remain.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains its mean-plus/minus-standard-deviation density summaries over 100 DIV2K test images. The additions introduce no new repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds substantial results for two further FRAMER instantiations. Its matched RealSR comparisons report PSNR of 23.45 versus 24.46 for TSD-SR and 24.36 versus 25.72 for SupResDiffGA. Figures 9–10 add weight trajectories, restoration examples, and image-level scores. These are newly reported results; existing Tables 1–5 and user-study values are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 5 changes the mathematical definition of FAW weights and removes the explicit sum-to-one property. This is a localized formal revision; the other mathematical definitions and objectives remain, with no added theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the standalone contribution concerning empirical analysis of the frequency hierarchy and explicitly qualifies that hierarchy as an empirical trend rather than a universal rule. The abstract, remaining contributions, and conclusion retain the central frequency-aware self-distillation and plug-and-play claims.

C2.justification: Beyond qualifying the hierarchy, new Appendix C interprets isolated FAW as prone to oversharpening and isolated FAM as lacking sufficient frequency-specific weighting. Appendix D interprets the added model results as evidence of broadly shared optimization challenges. The previous hallucination limitations and future-work discussion are retained in Appendix G.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures, degradation parameters in Table 6, frequency-mask radius, H200/batch-size information, computational measurements, and project link are retained. The added model comparisons assert matched protocols but provide no corresponding new concrete hyperparameter, training-budget, or access instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the same 53 referenced works are retained, including the substantive contrasts with frequency-aware learning and self-distillation methods. The newly evaluated baseline names do not accompany an expanded literature review or revised attribution to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and method-overview revisions, shortens the contribution list, updates author and affiliation information, and adds acknowledgements. New supplementary Sections C–D shift the former Sections C–E to E–G; most existing prose and narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the weight plots in Figure 9, component comparisons in Figure 10, and model-comparison Table 7. Existing supplementary displays are retained and renumbered. The title block is redesigned, and typography, display sizing, and page flow change without a wholesale redesign of the existing figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The added model comparisons and adaptive-module analyses strengthen empirical support, and the hierarchy qualification improves claim calibration. However, the substantial Equation 5 revision is not reconciled with retained benchmark values or surrounding normalization language. New Appendix C also claims the combined modules achieve every best perceptual score, although Figure 10 reports better NIQE for FAM alone on one example: 3.29 versus 4.03. These benefits coexist with unresolved methodological attribution and reporting inconsistencies, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
